record.original_question: Let K1 and K2 be fibred knots, and let (X_K1, omega_K1) and (X_K2, omega_K2) be the symplectic K3 knot-surgery manifolds obtained from them. If these symplectic manifolds are symplectomorphic, must K1 and K2 be equivalent knots?

evidence.quote: If K1, K2 are fibred knots and (XK1 , ωK1 ) is symplectomorphic to (XK2 , ωK2 ) are K1, K2 equivalent?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. Let E(2) denote the K3 surface, equipped with an elliptic fibration, and fix a section/cusp neighborhood that contains a smoothly embedded torus T of square zero. For a knot K in S^3, the Fintushel–Stern knot-surgery manifold X_K is defined as
   X_K = (E(2) \ ν(T)) ∪_φ (S^1 × (S^3 \ ν(K))),
where ν(·) denotes a tubular neighborhood and the gluing diffeomorphism φ: S^1 × ∂ν(K) → ∂(E(2) \ ν(T)) is chosen so that a longitude of K is matched with the boundary of a normal disk to T (the meridian of T), and so that S^1 × meridian(K) is glued to a push-off of T in T^2. When K is a fibred knot, the manifold X_K carries a natural symplectic form ω_K extending the standard Kähler/symplectic form on E(2), making (X_K, ω_K) a symplectic 4-manifold.

Question. Suppose K_1 and K_2 are fibred knots in S^3 and that the symplectic 4-manifolds (X_{K_1}, ω_{K_1}) and (X_{K_2}, ω_{K_2}) are symplectomorphic. Must K_1 and K_2 be equivalent knots in S^3?
artifact.status_search_result: The smooth analogue (X_{K_1} diffeomorphic to X_{K_2} implies K_1 equivalent to K_2) is a well-known conjecture of Fintushel–Stern that remains open in general; only partial results (e.g., for twisted fiber sums, certain families) are known. No source found that resolves the symplectic version for fibred knots; it appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fintushel–Stern knot surgery in torus bundles
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses the Fintushel–Stern knot surgery construction and conjecture that X_K determines K for fibred knots.
status_evidence.claim: The corresponding smooth/symplectic determination question is treated as an open conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Six Lectures on Four 4-Manifolds (Fintushel–Stern)
status_evidence.snippet: Knot surgery produces symplectic manifolds when K is fibred; the question of when X_{K_1} and X_{K_2} are equivalent remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference framing the problem as open.
